title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock
prompt:
You are given prices, where prices[i] is a stock's price on day i. Choose one day to buy and a later day to sell. Return the maximum profit you can make. If no profit is possible, return 0.

Write maxProfit(prices).

  • maxProfit([7, 1, 5, 3, 6, 4]) → 5 (buy at 1 on day 1, sell at 6 on day 4)
  • maxProfit([7, 6, 4, 3, 1]) → 0 (prices only fall)
  • maxProfit([]) → 0

Constraints: 0 <= prices.length <= 10^5, 0 <= prices[i] <= 10^4. So O(n²) is too slow: aim for one pass, O(n) time and O(1) extra space.

tests.name: cannot sell before buying (the max comes before the min)
a new low later can lead to a bigger profit
a longer generated input matches brute force

hints: Trigger: for each sell day, the best buy day is simply the cheapest day before it. The brute force inner loop keeps re-finding that minimum.
Idea: walk left to right once, carrying cheapestSoFar. At each day, the best profit if you sell today is price - cheapestSoFar.

Code shape: let cheapestSoFar = Infinity, best = 0; for (const price of prices) { best = Math.max(best, price - cheapestSoFar); cheapestSoFar = Math.min(cheapestSoFar, price); }. Update the profit before the minimum so you never buy and sell on the same day for a fake gain (here it would only ever be 0, but the order matters in many variants).
explain:
Time O(n), space O(1). One pass, two variables. The brute force was O(n²) because its inner loop recomputed the minimum of all earlier days for every sell day; carrying that minimum forward makes each day O(1).

How to say it: "Brute force tries every pair, O(n²). For each sell day the best buy is the cheapest earlier price, so I keep a running minimum while scanning once. That's O(n) time and O(1) space." This running-value idea is the simplest form of precomputation, which the prefix sums lesson builds on.
